findings.title: Error-only detection treats mixed and negated Discover queries as error queries
findings.body: The Discover eligibility check is a raw substring search for `event.type:error`, rather than determining that the query is restricted to errors. Queries such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, `!event.type:error`, or a search value containing that text will therefore be transformed to `upsampled_count()`. Those queries can include transactions, for which `sample_weight` is not applicable, producing incorrect totals (or a backend query error) for allowlisted projects. Parse/inspect the query conditions and only enable the transform when the effective event-type predicate excludes non-error events.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility is evaluated against the outer dataset instead of the dataset being queried
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset`, and the dashboard split path calls it with a different dataset (notably `discover` for the error half of a metrics-enhanced widget), but eligibility is checked with the closed-over `dataset`. As a result, an error split that is actually executed against Discover is treated as a metrics query and is never upsampled, even when its projects and query are eligible. The check should use `scoped_dataset` so the transformation corresponds to the query that will actually run.

findings.title: Process-randomized hash makes distributed cache invalidation ineffective
findings.body: The cache key embeds Python's built-in `hash()`, which is randomized per interpreter process. A key written by one web worker cannot be addressed by `invalidate_upsampling_cache` running in another worker, despite the helper documenting that invalidation keeps the cache consistent; each worker also misses entries populated by others. After an allowlist change, workers can consequently retain and use a stale eligibility decision until TTL expiry. Use a deterministic key component (for example a sorted, delimited ID string or a stable digest) so all processes share and invalidate the same key.
